title: you must install .NET Desktop Runtime torun this application.
summary: The merged Scoop packaging fix covers the original case. Newly merged #52038 restores MSI ownership of shared payloads instead of install-time copying, but no released-build resolution is established. Identify the remaining affected install before attributing it to a new defect.

next_action.label: Identify the still-affected installation
next_action.reason: Thanks for the continuing reports. The original Scoop packaging fix is merged, but an administrative MSI extraction skips installation steps and is not equivalent to a normal install. For the copy still failing, please give the exact PowerToys version, executable named in the prompt, installation path, and whether it came from updated Scoop, an official normal install, or extraction. This will distinguish missing bundled files from a separate runtime lookup problem; please do not install old runtimes or copy only a few DLLs for this comparison.

judgment.rationale: The merged Scoop packaging fix covers the original case. Newly merged #52038 restores MSI ownership of shared payloads instead of install-time copying, but no released-build resolution is established. Identify the remaining affected install before attributing it to a new defect.
evidence: Original Scoop 0.100 case was resolved by the official installer.
Scoop maintainers merged Extras #18020 and a user confirmed the updated package stopped prompts.
Later reports include official installers, administrative extraction, and mixed runtime versions; on November 16 a user still reports the prompt.
November 17 advice repeats manually copying three DLLs, which does not establish that the full runtime manifest is present.

Historical released installers copied the manifest payload during installation; the newly merged Smart Cabbing change removes that custom action and restores MSI file ownership: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/52038
